clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - Lauca National Park

Lauca can look very similar to other areas in the east Andes of northern Chile, but it’s recognizable for the iconic Volcán Parinacota, a tall snow-capped volcano that stands alone and away from other mountain ridges. text: Chilean phone codes will sometimes have a two digit area code in front, followed by seven digits. The patterns of the codes are easily memorable. Most of the central states also have different area codes for specific provinces, which can help you make accurate guesses.

clues.title: Pole: pole
text: Chile uses square concrete poles with an indent on both sides. They are somewhat similar to Brazilian poles, however have fewer horizontal supports in the indent. The upper part typically has small pinholes.
Wooden poles are also fairly common.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Sign: Empty slot under sign
text: Chile signs commonly have those empty slots at the top of signposts.

clues.title: Plate: Chile
text: Regular vehicles have white licence plates, while commercial and taxi vehicles have orange plates.
NOTE: Orange plates can also be seen in Ecuador. Brazilian commercial plates are red, but can look similar in some lighting.

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - A11 - Lluta River Valley
text: Along the Lluta River, the Ruta 11 passes through a wide valley lined by sloping, sandy mountains that often feature distinctly round rock protrusions. The valley is home to a large amount of agriculture relative to other parts of the Atacama Desert. You’ll often see sizable green fields lined by bushes, trees, or wooden fences, as well as bunches of planted Mexican fan palms. A railroad track also follows the Lluta River on both sides, so if you’re in a green valley next to both a river and a railroad, you’re almost certainly on Ruta 11.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Landscape - A11 - Barren
text: After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. This section of Ruta 11 features:
Many concrete barriers (which are often painted yellow), double guardrails, and roadside drainage ways.
Maroon-colored asphalt in some places.
Mountains are made of light reddish sand with occasional exposed rock. Rounded protrusions are also common
The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.

clues.title: Vegetation: Vegetation - Chilean Wine Palm
text: It is endemic to a small area of central Chile between southern Coquimbo, Valparaíso, Santiago, O'Higgins, and northern Maule regions. They are highly concentrated around Viña del Mar.
